# Herdr selection list: base the in-progress marker on work-item pane existence

## Problem statement

The "in progress" marker shown in the Herdr selection list is unreliable: it is
derived from the worklog `in-progress` status, which is maintained by the
hydrator — a self-healing loop that decides whether a claimed item is genuinely
being worked on. Every interactive/downtime dispatch now spawns an agent pane
whose **title carries the exact work-item ID** as a preserved trailing suffix
(`pane-title.ts`, `truncatePaneTitlePreservingSuffix`). The hydrator's active
detection must be a single simple rule: if there is a pane in this workspace
with the work item id (as part of) its title the item is being worked on; if
there is no such pane it is not.

> Producer review (2026-10-16): "This isn't reliable at present. review the
> algorith. It should be simple. Look for a pane in this workspace with the work
> item id as the title. If it exists then work item is busy. If it doesn't then
> it is not busy."
>
> An earlier revision matched the exact **label** of a workspace **tab**
> (`herdr tab list`). That proved unreliable: tabs are created by the dispatcher
> *anchor* as a placement side effect, so an item being dispatched can be
> evaluated before its tab exists (a false-demotion race), and tabs can be
> re-parented or renamed. Pane **titles** are set at spawn time, always carry
> the item ID as a preserved suffix, and survive re-parenting — matching them
> is the reliable signal this work item implements.

## Users

- Herdr operator selecting the next work item from the selection list.
- Downtime dispatcher / plugin panes that rely on the hydrator to release stale
  `in-progress` claims so the item re-enters the dispatchable pool.

Example user stories:

- As a Herdr operator, I want the selection list's in-progress marker to reflect
  reality — an item is "being worked on" iff a pane in my workspace has the
  work-item ID in its title — so I can trust the list without opening panes.
- As a dispatched agent, I want my claimed item left `in-progress` for as long
  as my work-item pane is open, so my claim is never released underneath me.
- As an operator, I want a stale claim (no work-item pane) released
  automatically and periodically so abandoned items return to the dispatchable
  pool.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An item is treated as actively worked **iff** a pane in the current
      workspace (`HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, or `herdr pane list --workspace <id>`)
      has a title **containing** the work-item ID (the dispatched pane titles
      always carry the ID as a preserved suffix). A pane title with no work-item
      ID contributes nothing. Verified by unit tests over a pure
      pane-title-matching helper.
- [ ] The hydrator's active detection is `herdr pane list --workspace <id>` +
      pane-title ID extraction; the pane-matching seam/types (`HydratorPane`,
      `listActivePanes`, `collectPaneWorkItemIds`, `isActivePaneMatch`) are used.
      Verified by code review + updated `hydrator.test.ts` (a `herdr pane list`
      spawn asserted; no `herdr tab list` spawn for active detection).
- [ ] Demotion rules are unchanged: a non-active item at stage `in_review` →
      `completed`/`in_review`; a non-active item with an active outbound blocker
      → `blocked`; otherwise → `open` (stage repaired to a compatible value). An
      item with a matching pane is never demoted. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] The signal is refreshed periodically from the selection list: the existing
      30 s hydrate task (`HYDRATOR_INTERVAL_MS`) and the hidden→visible
      focus-resume hook both re-evaluate pane existence, so a closed work-item
      pane clears the marker within one cadence and an opened pane keeps it.
      Verified by existing scheduler/visibility tests plus a pane-based
      hydration test.
- [ ] Fail-open preserved: an unavailable/unparseable `herdr pane list` aborts
      the cycle without demoting, and panes outside the current workspace never
      mark an item active. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries (notably the
      hydrator module header and the `pane-title.ts` rationale comment).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not change the worklog status/stage vocabulary or the demotion outcome
  rules.
- Keep the bounded/responsive hydrator contract (per-step timeout, per-tick
  cap, stdio isolation, fail-open) unchanged; only the "which items are active"
  lookup changes.
- Reuse the existing pane parsing/seam where possible rather than adding a
  second parser for the same CLI shape.
- Retain exports still used elsewhere: `extractWorkItemIdsFromText`
  (`ship-guard.ts`) and `isActiveBlocker` (`stalled-work.ts`).
- No CLI or socket API change; `herdr pane list` is already used by the plugin.
- Write in UK English; follow the project's test/build conventions.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — fetches `wl list --status in-progress`,
  fetches live panes (`herdr pane list [--workspace <id>]`), collects work-item
  IDs from pane titles (`collectPaneWorkItemIds`), and demotes items with no
  matching pane. Exposes pure helpers (`collectPaneWorkItemIds`,
  `isActivePaneMatch`, `decideDemotion`, `compatibleStage`, `isActiveBlocker`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — creates the hydrator runner with
  `workspaceId: process.env.HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, runs it every 30 s (`hydrate`
  task) and on hidden→visible focus-resume. The selection list's in-progress
  marker (`statusIcon(item.status)`) and Group N ordering (`status ===
  'in-progress'`) are driven by the worklog status this loop maintains plus the
  pane-based display marker (`applyActivePaneMarkers`).
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — truncation helpers that preserve the
  work-item ID as a trailing suffix so the pane-title match is always reliable.

## Desired change

The hydrator's "is this item active" signal is pane-title existence:

1. A pure helper returns the set of work-item IDs present in the current
   workspace's pane titles (`collectPaneWorkItemIds(tabs)` /
   `isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes)`).
2. `HydratorDeps.listActivePanes(workspaceId)` is backed by
   `herdr pane list --workspace <id>`.
3. `runHydrationOnce` uses pane membership; `decideDemotion`,
   `compatibleStage`, `isActiveBlocker`, `extractWorkItemIdsFromText` and the
   bounded-run machinery are unchanged.
4. Tests and the module/doc comments describe pane-title detection.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — pane-title matching seam/types/helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — hydrator wiring (workspace id, cadence,
  focus-resume, `active-pane-marker` task).
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — pane-title cases; exact, workspace-
  scope and fail-open cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.fixtures.ts` — pane fixtures + `pane list` exec
  router answer.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts` — updated to the
  pane-based deps.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — rationale comment for tile-title
  detection.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `applyActivePaneMarkers` production wiring.

## Related work

- WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI — Herdr hydrator: rescue `in_progress` work items with no
  active pane (parent of the hydrator design).
- WL-0MTF5WO2Q008B8US — Hydrator: demote stale `in_progress` items.
- WL-0MUY1CXSV008F8TZ / WL-0MUY1CYCB003DTKO / WL-0MUY1CYV6008BQWX — bounded/
  isolated hydrate steps (contract to preserve).
- WL-0MUKXFWLD006A8XI / WL-0MUYI3JAO002BTNL — item-ID tab anchor and dispatch
  wiring (tab-per-item convention; panes inherit the ID-titled anchor).
- WL-0MUY1CS9E006ZLS0 — re-based Herdr in-progress UI behaviour on `status`.
- WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9 — per-row agent-status icon (separate feature).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (scope):** "the logic for discovering when an item is being
  worked on" is the hydrator's active detection; the selection-list in-progress
  marker follows from the status the hydrator maintains plus the injected
  pane-title display marker.
- **Assumption:** pane titles carry the exact work-item ID as a trailing suffix
  for every dispatch path (manual, shell, downtime builders), so a
  contains-match is correct and robust; no substring false positives because the
  ID token is matched exactly.
- **Assumption:** `herdr pane list --workspace <id>` returns
  `result.panes[].label` (the pane title), as parsed by the shared
  `parseMachinePaneListOutput`; no new herdr capability is required.
- **Risk:** a pane may outlive its agent (kept open after the agent finishes),
  leaving an item `in-progress`. This matches the requested rule (pane = worked
  on); operators close the pane to release the item.
- **Scope-creep risk:** sharing the signal with `AgentTracker` or the
  agent-status icon is a linked follow-up item, not part of this change.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-10 — Created three children (core/verification/docs) and wired
  dependency edges.
- 2026-10-14 — Producer directed tab-label exact matching
  (commit 73463773).
- 2026-10-16 — Producer rejected the tab-label formulation as unreliable and
  directed pane-title matching: "Look for a pane in this workspace with the
  work item id as the title. If it exists then work item is busy." Rework
  updated the hydrator (tab-label → pane-title), the marker, tests, fixtures
  and docs accordingly.
data.title: Herdr selection list: base the in-progress marker on work-item tab existence

# Intake: Finish-gate live-repo guard trips on concurrent dev ref movement

**Work Item:** WL-0MV5MYBKJ0033P8U
**Issue Type:** bug
**Priority:** medium
**Discovered from:** WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish`'s live-repo mutation guard (`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` `snapshot_repo_state`/`diff_snapshots`, consumed by `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:guarded_run_all`) fails a full-suite run whenever any non-worktree ref moves during the ~17-minute run. On a multi-agent host, concurrent agent activity moves `refs/heads/dev` (another agent's finish fast-forward on the shared main checkout), `refs/remotes/origin/dev` and other `refs/remotes/origin/*` (concurrent fetch/push), and siblings' feature-branch refs — none of which the current exclusion covers. The result is a spurious 'live-repo mutation detected' verdict while the canonical suite itself passes, forcing a wasted ~17-minute run: the item resets to `open`, the agent must re-sync and re-warm the test cache before retrying. Observed twice on WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6.

## Users

- **Primary:** AI agents running `implement.py finish` or `/skill:test` on a shared multi-agent host; the guard's false positive blocks their release gate.
- **Secondary:** the human producer relying on the finish-gate verdict as the pre-push signal for `dev`.
- **Tertiary:** maintainers of `git_sandbox.py` and the two guards (F4 outer `run_tests.py`, F5 inner conftest/`live_repo_guard.py`) that share the helper.

Example user stories:

- As an **implementing agent**, I want the finish-gate full-suite run to stay green while sibling agents advance `dev`, fetch/push to `origin`, or move their own branch refs, so that concurrent activity on the shared host does not nullify a ~17-minute run.
- As a **producer**, I want the guard to keep failing on genuine in-place mutation of the guarded checkout (the SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX `GIT_DIR`-leak class), so real corruption is never reported as green.
- As a **maintainer**, I want the exclusion contract documented and regression-tested at both helper and guard level, so the two consumers cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — A snapshot diff in which **only** `refs/heads/dev`, `refs/remotes/origin/dev`, or `refs/remotes/origin/*` moved (working tree and non-excluded config unchanged) reports `changed == false`; `fingerprint()` agrees. Regression tests cover each ref class (local `dev`, remote-tracking `dev`, arbitrary `origin/*`).
- [ ] AC2 — Genuine mutations are **still** detected and fail the guard: a new/removed/moved ref outside the excluded set (e.g. fixture branch creation like the 2026-09-24 incident's `feature-x` / `wl-*-test`), a non-excluded local-config rewrite, and any working-tree change. No behaviour of the existing agent-worktree / `refs/worklog/*` exclusions regresses.
- [ ] AC3 — `guarded_run_all` (the `implement.py finish` test gate) and the inner per-test guard both pass in a deterministic regression test that moves `refs/heads/dev` and `refs/remotes/origin/dev` mid-run on a `tmp_path` sandbox, while the same harness still fails when a genuine mutation (e.g. a new non-excluded branch) is introduced.
- [ ] AC4 — The exclusion contract is documented in the `git_sandbox.py` module docstring and `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8, naming exactly which ref namespaces are excluded and why concurrent collaborative movement cannot be distinguished from suite-caused moves of those refs (residual-risk note).
- [ ] AC5 — Full project test suite (pytest + node, as declared by the test skill) passes with the new changes; new regression tests live with the existing guard tests (`tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py`, `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`, `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py` as appropriate).

## Constraints

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` remains **stdlib-only**, loadable by file location (repo-root `conftest.py` uses `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`; no `sys.path` mutation).
- Exclusions stay **derived from git plumbing**, never a `wl-*` name pattern (documented reason: a name pattern would also exclude the incident's own fixture branches).
- Snapshots stay **read-only**: only plumbing commands, never `gc`, `update-index`, `fetch` or `--refresh`.
- The fix must not silently disable detection of the SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX leak class (see AC2). Excluding a ref namespace is only acceptable where concurrent-agent movement and suite-caused movement are genuinely indistinguishable *and* the incident signature remains detectable through the other surfaces (working tree, config, non-excluded refs).
- Any extra git invocation must stay cheap and confined to the snapshot path; the per-test fingerprint must not become a full `status` scan.
- Implementation happens in the **SorraAgents** repo (the global-skills home where `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` lives), tracked via the ContextHub worklog — precedent: WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1 committed to SorraAgents.

## Existing state

- `snapshot_repo_state` captures refs (via `for-each-ref`, dropping `refs/worklog/*`), local config, registered worktrees and working-tree status; `diff_snapshots` filters out `excluded_refs` = branches checked out in worktrees under `<main_checkout>/.worklog/worktrees/` (union of both snapshots' sets) plus the `branch.<name>.remote`/`branch.<name>.merge` config those worktrees own.
- `main_checkout_root()` already anchors the exclusion on the main checkout so `implement.py finish` (which runs the suite from a linked worktree) excludes sibling worktrees — delivered by SA-0MUILGH5E007X627 / SA-0MUINEW6X0034C65.
- **Gap:** refs the shared host moves concurrently are not under `.worklog/worktrees/`, so they are not excluded: `refs/heads/dev` (main checkout's checked-out branch; another agent's finish fast-forwards it), `refs/remotes/origin/dev`, all other `refs/remotes/origin/*`, and any sibling feature branch not currently registered in a `.worklog/worktrees/` worktree.
- Observed on WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6: `refs/remotes/origin/dev` bbc8e89a → 4163175, `refs/heads/dev` advanced, and a sibling's feature-branch ref moved; both declared suite commands exited 0 yet the gate failed.

## Desired change

- Extend the exclusion contract so refs that concurrent agent activity legitimately moves cannot fail the gate: at minimum `refs/remotes/origin/*` (remote-tracking refs — only `fetch`/`pull`/`push` move them, never a hermetic fixture) and the integration branch `refs/heads/dev` (advanced by siblings' finish fast-forwards on the shared main checkout). Sibling feature-branch refs are already excluded while registered as agent worktrees; handle any residual unchecked-out sibling branch movement if the implementer can do so without a `wl-*` name pattern.
- Tighter alternative (if preferred by the implementer): scope the ref-check to the refs a suite could plausibly touch (e.g. ignore ref *moves* but still report ref *additions*), while keeping config + working-tree detection intact.
- Add regression tests at the helper level (`diff_snapshots`/`fingerprint`) and across both guards (`guarded_run_all` and the per-test conftest guard), using the existing hermetic `git_sandbox` factories under `tmp_path` — never the live checkout.
- Update `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §8 and the `git_sandbox.py` docstring to state the extended exclusion contract and the residual risk.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — Extend the exclusion set (e.g. `refs/remotes/origin/*`, `refs/heads/dev`) in `_parse_worktrees`/`snapshot_repo_state`/`diff_snapshots`/`fingerprint`; document the contract in the module docstring.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` — Helper-level regression tests for dev/remote-tracking ref movement (no diff) and non-excluded ref moves (still reported).
- `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` — Guard-level tests: mid-run `dev`/`origin/dev` movement does not trip the inner guard; a genuine non-excluded ref adds/moves still fails.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` / `skill/test/tests/test_guarded_run_all.py` — Verify `guarded_run_all` benefits from the shared fix; add a focused regression test if needed.
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — §8 exclusion contract update (refs excluded for concurrency reasons + residual risk).
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` — Only if the outer/inner guard needs a code change beyond the shared helper (prefer helper-only so consumers cannot drift).

## Related work

- `WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6` — source session where the false positive was observed twice (discovered-from).
- `SA-0MUILGH5E007X627` — predecessor false positive: linked-worktree anchoring; fixed by the `main_checkout_root()` helper this item builds on.
- `SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX` — 2026-09-26 `GIT_DIR` leak incident; the guard's reason to exist; the mutation-detection this item must not weaken.
- `SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63` — origin of `git_sandbox.py` (remote `dev` corruption / test isolation); snapshot design source.
- `SA-0MUG30J5F001L57H` / `SA-0MUG30JSE0069JEQ` — outer (`run_tests.py`) and inner (conftest) live-repo guards.
- `SA-0MUINEW6X0034C65` — superseding producer decision for the worktree-registration churn false positive (same guard path).
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — incident write-up and the snapshot/exclusion contract this item extends.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** excluding `refs/remotes/origin/*` and `refs/heads/dev` from the diff is acceptable because those refs' concurrent movement is indistinguishable from suite-caused movement, and exhaustive ref-based detection is replaced by config/working-tree/non-excluded-ref detection for those namespaces. If the producer prefers full-strength ref detection, the alternative is the tighter scoping (AC2 language) or running the suite under a repo lock.
- **Risk (false negative):** an overly broad exclusion hides a genuine incident signature. Mitigation: the incident class always also rewrites config and/or working tree (still detected); AC2 pins the incident signature detection.
- **Risk (scope creep):** expanding into refactoring the guard or adding a repo lock. Recorded as out of scope; a lock or serialisation idea can be linked as a follow-up work item.
- **Risk (performance):** the per-test fingerprint must stay cheap; any exclusion-list computation must not add a full `status` scan per test.
- **Risk (drift):** two consumers share the helper; keep the change helper-only so `run_tests.py` and the conftest guard cannot drift (AC3).
- **Residual risk:** two agents running `finish` concurrently can still contend on the same worktree/branch; excluded at the shared-ref level here, not solved (separate concern).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was required: the seed context (discovered-from:WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6) already contained the problem, observed evidence, impact, possible fix directions and a workaround. Questions below were resolved by repo investigation and recorded for auditability.

- Q: "Which repo owns the fix?" — Answer (agent, repo investigation): `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` and the guards live in the **SorraAgents** repo (global skills home; ContextHub's `skill/shared` is an untracked symlink to it). The work item is tracked in the ContextHub worklog; precedent WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1 was implemented and committed in SorraAgents with the item tracked from ContextHub. Evidence: `git ls-files skill/` in ContextHub (8 files, none under `skill/shared`), `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` of `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills` = SorraAgents, commit `6229a060` message.
- Q: "Can the fix simply ignore ref movement entirely?" — Answer (agent, analysis): the safer middle ground is excluding only concurrency-moved namespaces (`refs/remotes/origin/*`, `refs/heads/dev`) while keeping detection of new/removed non-excluded refs (fixture branches), config and working-tree changes — the incident signature never moves *only* `dev` without also changing config/tree. Recorded as an assumption (see Risks); preferred fix direction per the source item's "Possible fix".
- Q: "Does the inner per-test guard need its own change?" — Answer (agent, repo investigation): prefer a helper-only change; `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py` (F5) and `run_tests.py` (F4) both consume `fingerprint`/`diff_snapshots`, so a helper-level fix propagates to both without drift (SA-0MUINEW6X0034C65, §8.1 contract).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MS9PL90F002MR8G** – Fix legacy skill/ path refs in global ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md (completed)
- **WL-0MSUEO1U60072GNK** – Tests: identity gate unit + CLI suite (TDD red) (completed)
- **WL-0MRIEPH3J006RAPL** – wl sync corrupts dev branch when run from git worktree (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: active, advanced, agent, another, branch (+87 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: active, agent, another, branch, cache (+86 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: active, activity, agent, another, branch (+79 more)

> Automated matches are low-confidence (generic terms). The hand-curated related work above is authoritative.
data.title: Finish-gate live-repo guard trips on concurrent dev ref movement in multi-agent repos

# Intake Brief: Migrate downtime-worker tests from toHaveBeenCalledWith to observable-outcome assertions

**Work Item:** WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM
**Issue Type:** task
**Priority:** medium

## Problem statement

Parent **WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX** AC4 required assertions to prefer observable
outcomes over `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators
(`skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`). The 13-child split preserved all
existing assertions verbatim — **137** `toHaveBeenCalledWith` occurrences
before and after — and AC4 was deferred to this follow-up. The assertions are
therefore unreviewed: some legitimately assert the unit's observable contract
(calls to injected dependencies and boundary adapters), while others couple
tests to implementation detail (child-process event wiring) or duplicate a
behaviour already asserted through the returned outcome.

## Users

- **Maintainer / AI agent** — needs downtime-worker tests that survive
  refactoring because they assert the unit's observable contract rather than
  its internal wiring.
- **Reviewer** — needs an auditable classification showing every retained
  assertion is intentional and every migration preserves behavioural coverage.

## Evidence and baseline

Baseline across `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` (commit
`b195e01a`):

| File | `toHaveBeenCalledWith` occurrences |
|---|---|
| `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` | 37 |
| `downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` | 22 |
| `downtime-worker.critical-first.test.ts` | 21 |
| `downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts` | 15 |
| `downtime-worker.pane.test.ts` | 14 |
| `downtime-worker.test.ts` | 13 |
| `downtime-worker.sprint-view.test.ts` | 8 |
| `downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts` | 3 |
| `downtime-worker.settings.test.ts` | 2 |
| `downtime-worker.parse.test.ts` | 2 |
| **Total** | **137** |

(Includes 18 `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith` and 8 negative
`.not.toHaveBeenCalledWith` forms; 4 occurrences are `handle.once` child-process
event-wiring shape assertions.)

Targets are mock collaborators only — the files contain **zero** `vi.mock()`
calls. The overwhelming majority of occurrences target injected `deps.*`
functions (`spawnAgentPane` 34, `claimItem` 17, `rollbackClaim` 4,
`recordDispatch`/`recordDispatchFailure` 7, tier lookups, etc.) or test-local
mock adapters injected as dependencies. A small minority target non-boundary
internals (`handle.once`) or observable output streams (`stderrSpy`) or
injected adapters (`spawnFn`, `fetcher`, `callback`).

## Scope decision (producer, Q1-A)

The producer approved this classification rule:

- **Boundary / observable contract → retain (justified).** A call on an
  injected `deps` function or an injected boundary adapter
  (`spawnAgentPane`, `claimItem`, `closePane`, `spawnFn`, `fetcher`,
  `callback`, anchors, reapers, `dep`, …) is the unit's observable contract
  because the entry points take `deps` as an argument; there is no other
  observable channel for these side effects. Observable output streams
  (`stderrSpy`) are likewise observable outcomes.
- **Internal / redundant → migrate.** (a) Implementation-detail wiring such as
  `handle.once('error'|'exit', …)` shape assertions where the same test already
  drives the listener and asserts the resulting `spawned` outcome; (b)
  redundant call-shape/query assertions whose behaviour is already proven by a
  returned outcome/state (e.g. a tier query when `outcome.kind` and
  `outcome.candidate` are asserted).
- **Ordering assertions** (`toHaveBeenNthCalledWith` proving tier/fallback
  order) are retained unless an outcome assertion proves the identical
  ordering; otherwise they carry unique behavioural coverage.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Classification complete.** Every `toHaveBeenCalledWith` occurrence in
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` (baseline 137) is recorded in
   a classification table posted as a work-item comment — file, line, category
   (`retain` / `migrate`), and a one-line reason — and the category counts
   reconcile to the baseline total.
2. **Internal/redundant assertions migrated.** Every occurrence classified
   `migrate` is converted so the same behaviour is asserted through an
   observable outcome (returned value/state), or removed only where an
   existing assertion in the same test already proves that behaviour.
   Verification: `rg 'handle\.once\)\.toHaveBeenCalledWith'
   packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.test.ts` returns zero matches.
3. **Retained assertions justified.** Every retained occurrence carries a short
   inline comment stating why the dependency call is the unit's observable
   contract, and appears in the classification table (producer Q2-A).
4. **Behavioural coverage preserved.** No downtime-worker test case is deleted;
   the test-case count is unchanged; for every removed assertion the
   classification table names the outcome assertion that replaces it. Only
   `downtime-worker.*.test.ts` files change (no production-code change).
5. **Parent AC4 satisfied.** An evidence comment is posted on
   WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX linking this item and its outcome; the parent is not
   reopened or re-audited (producer Q3-A).
6. **Documentation and full suite.** All related documentation and code
   comments are updated to reflect the changes; the full project test suite
   passes with the new changes (run via `/skill:test`).

## Constraints

- Do not change production code — the change is confined to
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts` (plus inline comments).

  replacement or an explicit table justification.
- All written output in UK English.
- Do not introduce new test dependencies.
- CHANGELOG.md is out of scope (managed by the release pipeline).

## Existing state

- 14 `downtime-worker.*.test.ts` files (13 split files plus
  `downtime-worker.test.ts`), 137 `toHaveBeenCalledWith` occurrences, zero
  `vi.mock()` calls.
- Shared scaffolding (`makeDeps`, status fixtures, temp-dir helpers) lives in
  `downtime-worker.fixtures.ts`.
- Parent **WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX** is `completed`/`done`; AC4 was deferred to
  this item by producer decision.

## Desired change

Apply the producer-approved classification to every occurrence, migrate the
internal/redundant subset to observable-outcome assertions, annotate the
retained subset, publish the classification table, and close the deferred
parent AC4 with an evidence comment.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — largest target (37); mostly boundary deps + redundant `getNextItem` queries
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` — boundary deps, `stderrSpy`, ordering assertions

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: over-migration weakens regression coverage.** Mitigation: every
  removal must be paired with the outcome assertion that replaces it, named in
  the classification table.
- **Risk: mechanical removal of ordering assertions hides tier-ordering
  regressions.** Mitigation: retain `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith` ordering
  assertions unless an outcome assertion proves identical ordering.

- **Risk: scope creep.** Do not migrate `toHaveBeenCalledWith` outside

- **Risk: classification ambiguity.** Unresolved cases are retained with an

# F1: Classification and replacement audit (toHaveBeenCalledWith)

**Parent:** WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM
**Issue type:** task (verification-first — the analysis gate for the migration)

## Goal

Produce the authoritative classification table (parent AC1) covering **all 137**
`toHaveBeenCalledWith` occurrences across the 14 `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.*.test.ts`
files, post it as a work-item comment, and prove that every `migrate` occurrence has a
named observable-outcome replacement (parent AC4's replacement-traceability requirement).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Classification table published** — a comment on WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM with one row per
  occurrence: file, line, category (`retain` / `migrate`), and a one-line reason.
- **Baseline reconciled** — the 137 rows reconcile exactly to the documented per-file baseline
  (dispatch 37, audit-tier 22, critical-first 21, tiers 15, pane 14, downtime-worker.test 13,
  sprint-view 8, orchestrator 3, settings 2, parse 2), including the 18
  `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith` and 8 `.not.toHaveBeenCalledWith` forms.
- **Producer rule applied** — classification follows the producer-approved rule
  (WL-0MV5RYKQD000L5LM, plan Q1 answer **A**): retain calls on injected `deps`/boundary
  adapters (`spawnAgentPane`, `claimItem`, `closePane`, `spawnFn`, `dep`, anchor/reaper
  lookups, …), observable output streams (`stderrSpy`), injected `fetcher` / `onProxyIdle`
  `callback` (sole observable channel for the asserted effect), and `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith`
  ordering assertions unless an outcome assertion proves identical ordering; migrate
  `handle.once('error'|'exit', …)` shape wiring where the same test drives the listener and
  asserts the resulting `spawned` outcome, plus redundant query-call assertions whose
  behaviour is already proven by a returned outcome/state.
- **Replacements named** — every `migrate` row names the observable-outcome assertion
  (existing, or to be added in F2) that replaces it.
- **No silent drops** — category counts per file sum to the baseline total; no occurrence
  is omitted.

## Constraints

- Analysis and table only — **no test-file edits in this step**.
- UK English throughout.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — 37 occurrences (largest)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` — 22 occurrences, stderrSpy rows
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.critical-first.test.ts` — 21 occurrences
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.test.ts` — 14 occurrences, 4 `handle.once` wiring rows
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.tiers.test.ts` — 15 occurrences (Nth ordering rows)

## Deliverables

- Work-item comment with the reconciliation-checked classification table
- Data (comment id) for F3 to consume and F4 to verify against
